body:
ariane: Quick Q from my team - one of our ICs had an unexpected hospitalization in Nov and missed the entire year-end shutdown. They have ~12 unused PTO days. Are payouts automatic or can we convert to carryover due to medical LOA?
devin: Standard flow auto-pays unused PTO on Jan payroll. But medical LOA overlapping the shutdown can be an exception if we get docs and file before payroll cutoff.
cleo: I already uploaded hospital discharge paperwork to the HR portal and my manager added a note. I would prefer to take the days next year vs a payout.
peopleops: Thanks @cleo. Please submit the HR Exception form here: https://intranet.redwood/hr/forms/pto-exception and attach the LOA docs + manager confirmation. Include exact PTO days requested to carry.
ariane: For clarity, what's the internal label if approved? Do we create a separate bucket or simply stop the payout?
peopleops: We mark approved days as "temporary carryover" and add a payroll memo so it isn't auto-paid. It shows as a Q1-only balance and expires end of March unless scheduled.
payroll-bot: Automated reminder: Payroll cutoff to halt year-end PTO payouts is 2024-12-12 16:00 PT. Submissions after cutoff may not be reversible.
devin: Also flag to Finance: any exception >5 days requires finance annotation because of accrual accounting.
cleo: Understood. Submitted the form and attached docs. Manager note says medical LOA 2024-11-08 to 2024-12-22.
peopleops: Got it. I'll acknowledge receipt and route to Payroll and Finance for review. Expect a decision within 3 business days unless exec signoff required.
ariane: Thanks, looping back once approved. :thumbsup:
cleo: Appreciate it, thank you everyone.
peopleops: If anyone else has similar cases, please cc People Ops early so we can pause autopay triggers before cutoff.
